report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/ceiling.py: classification arms, summary, ceiling, render, main. Claims mostly kept; noted docstring/render mismatch on reopen threshold and uncheckable materiality rationale.
risks: render_ceiling | medium | Docstring says 'honest-framing render' but render omits alias_probe_failures when zero and does not print n_scored_clean; also prints 'reopen signal' based on reopen_temporal_lane without showing n_tasks_reachable_clean, potentially misleading. | Compare rendered lines against result dict; decide if omissions are acceptable.

temporal_ceiling | medium | Comment claims 'None parents == probe failed / no sha; [] cannot happen for a resolvable sha' — this is not verified in this chunk; risk of relying on an invariant not enforced here. | Inspect parent extraction in prior chunk or caller.

main | low | ASCII render with UnicodeEncodeError fallback writes to stdout.buffer, but if print(text) partially writes before error, partial output may appear; risk of duplicated or interleaved output. | Test with a terminal that raises UnicodeEncodeError mid-print.

render_ceiling | low | Static_hits computed from summary_clean and summary_leaky; if both have STATIC_EDGE same labels, they are double-counted in the message, but that's cosmetic. | Check if double-counting is intended.

handoff.purpose: Review classification arms, summary, ceiling computation, render, and CLI entry point.

symbols.name: _def_count
symbols.note: Inner function returning count_of; counts aliases for a definition in a given arm revision.

symbols.name: _summary
symbols.note: Aggregates class counts across per_task for a given key (classes_clean or classes_leaky).

symbols.name: _ceiling
symbols.note: Computes REACHABLE share over a denominator; returns 0.0 if denominator is zero.

symbols.name: render_ceiling
symbols.note: Renders ASCII text summary; includes static-edge warnings, reachable audit, and reopen signal.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry: parses --min-count, calls temporal_ceiling, prints render with ASCII fallback.

claims.why: Rendered text is all ASCII; fallback encodes to ASCII with replacement. Honest-framing is subjective but the render surfaces caveats (static edges, alias probe failures, merge commits).

claims.text: This is a walk-forward BACKTEST HIT-RATE (best case for temporal coupling), NOT slicer recall
claims.why: The render labels the metric as ceiling and distinguishes from recall; the computation uses backtest revisions and counts REACHABLE labels.

claims.text: the gap between the two arms is the self-prediction artifact: coupling that exists only because the minted commit is counted
claims.why: The clean arm excludes the mint commit, leaky includes it; the difference is attributed to the mint commit's inclusion.

claims.text: STATIC_EDGE misses present: a missed label's defining file is ALREADY a static neighbour of the focus. That is edge-but-dropped -- a slicer defect, strictly more important than anything temporal.
claims.why: Renders a warning and lists tasks with STATIC_EDGE in classes_clean; the claim about importance is a policy statement, not checkable.

claims.text: clean-arm REACHABLE labels (audit these -- each is a claim that pre-mint history named the file)
claims.why: Lists REACHABLE labels from classes_clean; the claim that they indicate pre-mint history is consistent with the clean arm's definition.

claims.text: clean arm is first-parent history only
claims.why: Rendered note for merge commits; the backtest uses sha^ which is the first parent.

claims.text: no backtest rev ... clean arm not scored
claims.why: Renders backtest_rev_reason; when absent, classes_clean is set to NO_BACKTEST_REV or the task is excluded.

claims.text: rename-alias probe(s) failed: those files were scored rename-BLIND and the ceiling may be understated
claims.why: Renders when alias_probe_failures is truthy; the understatement risk is consistent with the comment in temporal_ceiling.

claims.text: REOPEN signal: clean rename-aware ceiling clears the materiality floor (share OR breadth) -- the temporal-enrichment lane may be worth reopening
claims.why: Renders when reopen_temporal_lane is true; the condition uses REOPEN_MIN_SHARE and REOPEN_MIN_TASKS, matching 'share OR breadth'.

claims.text: measured at min_count=1, BELOW the reopen threshold: a single co-occurrence is one data point, not a pattern (churn.py). The reopen condition is defined at min_count >= 2.
claims.why: Renders when min_count < 2 and reopen_temporal_lane is true; the statement about the threshold is a policy claim, not directly checkable, but the min_count check is present.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- N clean-reachable label(s) in M task(s) is below the materiality floor
claims.why: Renders when reopen_temporal_lane is false and n_reach > 0; the numbers come from summary_clean and n_tasks_reachable_clean.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- clean ceiling is zero; the temporal lane stays closed.
claims.why: Renders when n_reach is zero; consistent with ceiling_clean being zero.

claims.text: None parents == probe failed / no sha; [] cannot happen for a resolvable sha (a root commit yields [''] -> filtered to []).
claims.why: The parent extraction logic is not in this chunk; the invariant is asserted but not verifiable here.

claims.text: The lane A2 reopen trigger, stated by the machine so a future session cannot misread the close: the clean rename-aware ceiling must clear the materiality floor (share OR breadth), not merely be non-zero -- the 2026-07-21 close measured exactly one recoverable label, and one label must read as 'stay closed' (see REOPEN_MIN_* rationale).
claims.why: The REOPEN_MIN_* constants and the historical close are not in this chunk; the trigger logic is present but the rationale is external.
main only computes and prints; no writes or side effects.

observations.what: render_ceiling docstring claims 'honest-framing' but when alias_probe_failures is zero, the render omits that line entirely, and it never prints n_scored_clean; the reopen signal line depends on reopen_temporal_lane which is computed with REOPEN_MIN_* constants not visible here.
The comment in temporal_ceiling says '[] cannot happen for a resolvable sha' but this chunk does not verify parent extraction; the invariant is asserted without evidence in this window.

main's UnicodeEncodeError fallback writes to stdout.buffer after print(text) may have partially written; if the error occurs mid-print, partial output could be followed by a full ASCII version, causing duplication.
render_ceiling computes static_hits by summing STATIC_EDGE counts from both arms; if the same label appears in both arms, it is double-counted in the warning, but that is cosmetic.
